question: While the EU maintains a policy of sanctions and diplomatic restrictions on Belarus, several recent developments raise questions about the coherence and effectiveness of this approach.

In 2025, the Belarusian authorities carried out a series of clemency measures: 156 prisoners were released, including 123 in December, among whom were nationals of several EU Member States, as well as citizens of partner countries, such as the United States and the United Kingdom.

These decisions were presented by the Belarusian authorities as humanitarian gestures, but also as political signals aimed at promoting a gradual normalisation of international relations and contributing to the stabilisation of the situation in Europe. The US has initiated a review of its sanctions regime, lifting some sanctions against the Belarusian potash fertiliser sector.
In this context, could the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy answer the following questions: 1.
Does she believe that the EU’s current position on Belarus remains fully in line with geopolitical realities and Europe’s strategic interests?

Does she envisage a gradual and conditional evolution of this policy, given the potential role that Belarus could play as a facilitator in seeking a negotiated solution to the conflict between Russia and Ukraine?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.1.2026) The EU’s policy on Belarus is guided by the Council conclusions of 19 February 20241 and 12 October 20202. The EU welcomes the recent releases of political prisoners, following diplomatic engagement by the US.
Nevertheless, more than 1 000 political prisoners remain arbitrarily detained, repression continues and no substantial improvement in the overall human rights situation can be observed.

Since August 2020, the EU has adopted several rounds of restrictive measures against Belarus3 in response to the repression of civil society and democratic opposition, misconduct of the electoral process, the incitement and organisation of illegal border crossings, human rights violations, the diverting of a passenger flight, hybrid activities against Member States, and the regime’s involvement in Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine.

The role of Belarus as a partner in Russia’s war will continue to be assessed with due diligence, and any violations of international law and human rights must be duly investigated and brought to justice. The EU will continue to support the democratic aspirations of the Belarusian people and condemn the illegal actions of the regime, remaining steadfast in its support for a democratic Belarus.
